raw_case_text:
In 2009, a 6-year-old boy presented with abdominal pain, constipation, and encopresis. Imaging revealed intussusception that was only temporarily reduced with air enemas, necessitating an emergency laparotomy that revealed a causative ileocecal valve mass. On microscopic examination, the mass consisted of non-granulomatous hyperplastic lymphoid tissue that was determined to be non-neoplastic by immunohistochemistry and fluorescent in situ hybridization. Surgical resection resolved the symptoms, but in the context of the patient's medical history the lymphoid hyperplasia could not simply be ascribed to infection. His birth and past medical history revealed that after an uneventful term gestation and delivery, his development was unremarkable until cessation of breastfeeding at 2 years of age, after which he began to experience recurrent episodes of otitis media and sinusitis. That year he developed pulmonary symptoms that required a hospitalization and which eventually led to the development of bronchiectasis. Throughout the following 3 years, he continued to experience upper respiratory infections and recurrent otitis media with hearing impairment secondary to tympanic membrane rupture for which he underwent bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tube placement, tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy, and sinus evacuation.
Pertinent negative testing included Histoplasma serology, total complement activity, sweat chloride testing for cystic fibrosis, granulocyte oxidative burst testing for chronic granulomatous disease, and a tracheal cilia biopsy for ciliary dyskinesia. Quantitative total immunoglobulin and immunoglobulin subclass assays were repeatedly within normal limits except for consistently elevated levels of IgM (Table 1). However, while he demonstrated adequate functional response to protein antigens, despite repeated vaccination with conjugate pneumococcal vaccine and the pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccines, his pneumococcal titers were suboptimal, indicating functional antibody deficiency. Flow cytometric quantitative analysis of lymphocytes revealed a reduced number of T cells and a persistently decreased CD4:CD8 ratio. He had a low normal number of B cells, mildly low number of memory B cells, and a proportionately mild decrease in class-switched memory B cell subset (Table 1), but without evidence of class-switch blockage. His T cell function assay demonstrated evidence of impairment with low response to mitogens, normal response to Candida antigen, and no response to tetanus antigen. Testing for toll-like receptor function and the mannan-binding lectin pathway was unremarkable. Replacement subcutaneous gammaglobulin therapy was started in light of his history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections causing significant morbidity, functional antibody deficiency, and diminished T cell numbers and function. He subsequently developed significant cervical and occipital lymphadenopathy that was non-tender and not associated with any systemic symptoms, suggestive of infectious etiology.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 6-year-old boy presented with acute abdominal pain, constipation, and encopresis, on a background of recurrent sinopulmonary infections and otitis media since age 2 years.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In 2009, the child presented with abdominal pain, constipation, and encopresis due to intussusception that failed air-enema reduction and required emergency laparotomy for an ileocecal valve mass. Since weaning from breastfeeding at age 2 years, he had suffered recurrent otitis media (complicated by tympanic membrane rupture and hearing loss), recurrent sinusitis, and lower respiratory tract infections leading to bronchiectasis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recurrent otitis media with tympanic membrane rupture and hearing impairment, recurrent sinusitis, pneumonia, and bronchiectasis since age 2 years. Past surgical history: bilateral myringotomy with tympanostomy tubes, tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy, and sinus evacuation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for abdominal pain, constipation, encopresis, and chronic/recurrent sinopulmonary and ear infections.

objective.physical_examination: Later developed non-tender cervical and occipital lymphadenopathy without systemic symptoms.
objective.routine_investigations: Histoplasma serology, total complement activity, sweat chloride test, and granulocyte oxidative burst assay (for CGD) all negative/normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal imaging & emergency laparotomy: ileocolic intussusception caused by an ileocecal valve mass; histopathology, IHC, and FISH showed benign non-granulomatous hyperplastic lymphoid tissue. Tracheal cilia biopsy: negative for ciliary dyskinesia. Immunological workup: persistently elevated IgM with normal total IgG/IgA/IgG subclasses, suboptimal pneumococcal polysaccharide/conjugate vaccine titers (functional antibody deficiency), reduced total T cells and persistently decreased CD4:CD8 ratio, mildly decreased memory and class-switched memory B cells, impaired T-cell mitogen and tetanus antigen proliferation (normal Candida response), and normal TLR and mannan-binding lectin pathways.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Combined primary immunodeficiency (functional specific antibody deficiency, persistent hyper-IgM, CD4:CD8 inversion, and T-cell dysfunction) presenting with ileocecal lymphoid hyperplasia/intussusception and bronchiectasis (histoplasmosis ruled out by negative Histoplasma serology). Confirmation: Ileocecal mass histopathology/IHC/FISH showing non-neoplastic lymphoid hyperplasia and comprehensive quantitative/functional lymphocyte and antibody assays. Plan & clinical course: Underwent surgical resection of the ileocecal valve mass (resolving the intussusception) and initiated replacement subcutaneous immunoglobulin therapy.
